tells: 1. Face close is waxy CG: flat orange skin with no subsurface or pores, low-poly jaw/neck silhouette, glassy unfocused eyes, and a pearl necklace that floats off the skin; the out-of-focus woman at left is a flat-shaded mannequin (club-4-face.png, centre face and left third)

2. Front row in the wide is a lineup: every visible person sits upright with both hands on the table, facing camera, so the row reads as posed, not watching a show (club-1-wide.png, lower-middle band across all four tables)

3. Laugh start is weak and late: through 12.0-12.4 nobody changes, then only the white-shirt and blonde women open their mouths by 12.6-13.0 while the back rows and the left half stay still; the build reads as a cue, not a ripple (club-5-strip.png, frames 4-6, right two tables and background rows)

4. Back rows are dark, stiff, evenly spaced silhouettes with near-identical upright heads, plus a figure standing dead centre in front of the lit bar sign like a cutout (club-1-wide.png and club-2-mid.png, upper-middle band and bar sign)

5. Material/edge tells: a dark smeared patch on the grey skirt, hard-edged bright candle glasses with no bloom falloff on hands, and a cropped bright arm at the right frame edge (club-6-held.png, lower centre skirt; club-2-mid.png, right edge)

1. Second and later rows look like standing mannequins: upright torsos, arms hanging straight at the sides, heads at one height, no seat contact, a grid of statues (theatre-1-wide.png and theatre-6-held.png, middle and back rows, left and right edges)
2. Laughs read as screams: wide square open mouths with no cheek raise or eye squint on the front-row men and women (theatre-2-mid.png, front row left-centre; theatre-3-mid.png, centre)

3. Face close: helmet-like hair with no strands, painted brows, uniform plastic skin, and a hand with over-long, boneless fingers floating near the chin; the blurred figures behind are flat low-poly shapes (theatre-4-face.png, whole face and hand at left-centre)

4. Twisted or collapsed postures: the teal-hoodie man folded down staring into his lap like he is ill, and the beanie man at the right head-down with a hard helmet hair shell (theatre-6-held.png, front row centre; theatre-3-mid.png, bottom right)

5. Large empty black regions left and right of the lit block plus hard spill cut-off make the house feel like a lit patch in a void; the back rows are crushed to grey-blue silhouettes with no depth gradient (theatre-1-wide.png, left and right thirds; theatre-5-strip.png, right side of every frame)

1. Hair-card alpha break-up: a stippled, dithered, jagged hair edge on the yellow-shirt man and a torn, floating hair cap on the afro man; these shimmer in motion and are the clearest CG tell (openmic-4-face.png, right side of the hair; openmic-6-held.png, top of the centre-right head)
2. Smeared, low-res clothing textures with hard UV seams: a white smear on the navy hoodie and blurred denim on the jacket (openmic-6-held.png, left figure torso; openmic-2-mid.png, left edge)

3. The wide is a dense clump all facing camera with hands on knees, and two standing figures at the back stiff as cutouts; the flat glowing door panel looks like an untextured card (openmic-1-wide.png, centre crowd, back left, door at left)

4. Laughs are good on two people (bob-haired woman, green-top woman) but the yellow-shirt and denim men stay neutral in every frame, and the 12.0-12.4 frames are nearly identical, so the start of the laugh lacks a lead-in (openmic-5-strip.png, frames 1-3 and the men at left-centre)

5. Faces at mid distance are mannequin-smooth with shiny foreheads and a fixed gaze; the background blonde's hand floats in front of her chest without contact (openmic-4-face.png, right background; openmic-3-mid.png, right-side faces)
